image_description: A close-up, top-down view of a single loudspeaker driver (woofer). The image features a textured black cone with concentric ridges, a gold-colored dust cap in the center with a distinct mesh or honeycomb texture, and a black rubber surround connecting the cone to the outer frame. The background is dark and out of focus, emphasizing the speaker component.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The gold dust cap has a very regular, almost digitally generated honeycomb/mesh pattern that lacks the subtle irregularities of real metal mesh or fabric. It appears slightly 'painted on' rather than physically textured.
Slight softness/blur at the extreme edges of the visible cone, likely due to depth-of-field simulation, but borders on looking like generation blur rather than optical bokeh.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific type of speaker component (woofer vs subwoofer) and verify material classification (paper vs polypropylene).
To analyze the micro-texture of the cone and dust cap for signs of AI smearing or repetitive pattern artifacts.
To ensure the rubber surround connects seamlessly to both the cone and the frame without melting or boundary bleeding.
To verify the convex curvature of the dust cap is geometrically consistent with lighting highlights.

focus_areas: Texture consistency of the gold dust cap (mesh pattern realism)
Boundary sharpness between the rubber surround and the cone
Lighting reflection coherence on the curved surfaces
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the 'honeycomb' texture on the central gold dome. Real speaker dust caps often have dimples or smooth surfaces, but this specific regular grid pattern is a common AI artifact when trying to render mesh. Check if the lighting highlights on the dome match the supposed curvature.
